searchText: hi! quick question that is more dev-related: will we have a way to monitor how many incoming transactions are native 1559 vs "legacy" transactions converted to the 1559 format? it'd be useful to have this statistic to measure the progress of dapps and wallets implementing 1559 They wont be converted, their encoded representation will remain the same. They will only be interpreted using 1559 rules. So it will simple to distinguish them. If they have a gas price field set then it is a legacy transaction However in clients we can definitely implement metrics to measure this evolution. So, how should block explorers display them, in your opinion? Should they be show as legacy or regular txns? There should be a distinction in my opinion Maybe you add details next to the effective gas price and keep a single line. gas price is always the effective gas price, regardless of the transaction type, and you have additional info with details either directly or if you click on see more Once we have the YOLO net up, we should show it to Etherescan too and ask what they think 🙂 yeah makes sense What commit hash should I use for the client integration devnet? Do we want to make a change to the EIP to raise the initial BASE FEE to 100 gwei before we do it? Why do we want to raise the base fee? To reflect network status?(mainnet) I still weakly prefer 1. Failing fast is preferable, and if the network can't handle 20 minutes of price escalation it is better to know while people are watching then at a random point in time later. I forget who mentioned during ACD that 1559 should have blockchain reference tests. I have been focusing on general state reference tests for now, but if anybody has suggestions for test cases that necessitate multiple blocks please share To reduce the number of 200% blocks right after the fork, yes. We can't get the "exactly right" base fee, of course, but we're likely ~100x off right now. I assume we want to see the BASE FEE going down to its minimum, then back up. Also, if possible, we should test the transition from pre-BASE FEE blocks to ones with a BASE FEE (i.e. the fork transition). both of those make sense to me Would it be possible to open a draft PR against ethereum/tests? It would be nice to follow along will do. I have been focused on getting a green test against besu before opening a draft pr, but since the failures have been for general state tests, I can go ahead and start a draft pr. Is there value in having both general state tests and blockchain tests? The bar is definitely lower for state tests Yeah this makes sense. Maybe want to even set it too high so we start with <50% blocks. Of course hard to estimate yeah, I don't think we can get it quite right, but we can definitely get it "order of magnitude" right: 10 is too low, 1000 is too high, 100 is a happy middle > To reduce the number of 200% blocks right after the fork, yes. It will happen sooner or later anyway, what’s the point? If we start it at 100, we may actually never see a 100x increase/decrease in base fee! Hm, would it be fine to start at 100 gwei for testnets, and any other network that uses it, too? Hopefully so. I would hate to see 1559 parameterized differently in different networks. Alternatively, it could be based on the minimum gas fee in the parent block, or `max(1 gwei, min(parent block gas prices))` I think we're a lot worse off if we over-price than under-price, though. So I'm still 👍 with the simple 1 gwei. what's the motivation for including the `effectiveGasPrice` in the tx receipt?
